jobs.title: Financial Management Consultant
jobs.description:

Travel Required :
Up to 10%

What You Will Do :
Guidehouse is currently seeking a professional consultant in support of our federal law enforcement client. The Consultant will lead and support key business process improvement initiatives, transform complex data into clear and meaningful insights, enhance business operations through automation and tool development, and strengthen organizational effectiveness by contributing to clear communication plans and coordinated training efforts. This role provides critical knowledge management, end‑user support, and solution delivery to help drive operational excellence across the enterprise.

Responsibilities of this role are as follows, to include but not limited to:
- Provide clear, actionable insights to leadership by gathering and analyzing data, developing comprehensive reports, and presenting findings and recommendations
- Ability to quickly synthesize information, learn new skills, approach problems with a range of solutions, and lead client-facing discussions and meetings
- Contribute to business process improvement and automation efforts to enhance efficiency and effectiveness across the organization
- Create customized tools and reports, including advanced Excel models and PowerPoint presentations
- Support the development and execution of communication plans and organizational rollout activities
- Assist in the development and delivery of training initiatives for enterprise-wide systems and processes.
- Provide knowledge management support by developing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), step-by-step guides, and user documentation for a variety of stakeholders.
- Deliver customer‑focused end-user support by identifying issues, conducting root-cause analysis, and helping troubleshoot solutions.

What You Will Need :
- An ACTIVE and MAINTAINED "TOP SECRET" Federal or DoD security clearance.
- Bachelor’s Degree; FOUR (4) years of additional professional experience may be used in lieu of a degree
- TWO (2) or more years of consulting experience.

What Would Be Nice To Have :
- Experience with Microsoft Power BI to develop dashboards, visualizations, and data‑driven insights
- Experience with SharePoint for content management, collaboration, and workflow support
- Knowledge of the Federal Travel Regulation (FTR)

jobs.title: Strategy & Transformation Managing Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Family :
Strategy & Transformation Consulting
Travel Required :
None
Clearance Required :

What You Will Do :
Strategy and Transformation Managing Consultants help our clients transform their business processes, develop and implement organizational strategies and cultural transformations, improve efficiency and operations, increase transparency and performance management, and comply with Federal laws and regulations. As a managing consultant, you will be a leader within our project and account teams, helping our clients solve complex public health and business challenges from strategy through execution. In this role you will drive our client engagements, mentor junior staff, and help shape the market’s business development and market strategies.

As a managing consultant, you will have an opportunity to deepen your specialized knowledge and consulting skills, with room for long-term professional growth and career development within the firm. We are looking for candidates who are self-motivated, outcomes oriented, and prepared to deliver compelling, high impact solutions to our federal health clients' toughest organizational and programmatic challenges.

Job Description/Responsibilities
- Lead end-to-end project delivery for management consulting projects, from project initiation, through analysis, solutions development, implementation, and closeout; projects can span organizational development and transformation, strategic planning and implementation, business process improvement, risk management, and change management and strategic communications, as well as direct-mission support to federal health clients

- Foster and sustain meaningful client relationships, identify client needs, and develop solutions to address these needs

- Scope projects to meet client requirements and develop work plans that reflect project scope and client expectations

- Play a key role in staffing projects, including identifying internal staff and interviewing external candidates

- Provide end-to-end oversight and quality control for development of client solutions and work products, such as root cause and gap analysis, findings and recommendation reports, requirements documents, Visio process flows, standard operating procedures, strategic plans, strategic communications, and reporting dashboards

- Facilitate large and small group meetings and working sessions, including for executive level clients, to gather requirements, identify paint points, develop strategies, and built team culture

- Develop and implement strategic communication, staff engagement, change management, and organizational development strategies in support of transformation initiatives

- Deliver high-quality client service in a fast-paced, unpredictable environment

- Build positive team culture and working environment, mentor and develop staff, and provide regular feedback to team members

- Understand and monitor engagement financials

- Understand and use firm capabilities, solutions, and methodologies

- Contribute to a pipeline of new business through active relationship development/management, proposal efforts, and thought leadership

What You Will Need :
- Bachelor’s degree

- 6+ years professional experience

- 3+ years consulting or client service experience

- Experience at or supporting federal health (i.e., HHS, CDC) or other governmental agencies

- Experience leading projects, including establishing and managing work plans

- Experience leading a team of 4+ staff

- Experience in strategy, organizational transformation, organizational development, process improvement, workforce strategy, change management, communications, monitoring and evaluation, or emergency response and preparedness

- Demonstrated ability to use data and AI to inform strategy, problem-solve, and make decisions

What Would Be Nice To Have:
- Master’s Degree (e.g., MBA, MPH, MPP, MHA, MPA, MSOD)

- Change management, facilitation, coaching, process improvement, or project management certification (e.g., Lean Six Sigma Green or Black Belt, CAPM, PMP, CCMP, or Prosci)

- Ability to think strategically while delivering tactically, with a keen attention to detail

- Ability to investigate, make sense of, and break down complex client challenges into clear, digestible approaches and solutions

- Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain strong business relationships with senior executives

- Experience leading and facilitating meetings, trainings, or workshops with executive-level clients

- Excellent written and verbal communications skills with a demonstrated ability to make difficult concepts easy to understand

- Experience conducting organizational assessments, developing strategic plans, and making recommendations for improvement

- Experience with delivering high-quality client service in a fast-paced, unpredictable environment

jobs.title: Managing Consultant-Energy Markets
jobs.description:
Job Family :
Power Systems Engineering Consulting
Travel Required :
Up to 25%
Clearance Required :
None

What You Will Do :

The Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team’s work supports developers, operators and sponsors to bring in new grid-scale and community renewables, storage and green fuels resources. The Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team assists utilities and large commercial companies in their ESG, decarbonization and renewable integration efforts.

Our Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team develops and maintains a suite of quantitative market models that Guidehouse’s clients, renewable and storage players, and utilities depend on for capital investment decisions, business improvement and grid reliability. Through our wholesale and retail market expertise and modeling capabilities, we forecast energy market conditions across North America, along with generating resource additions and retirements, intra-day commercial optimization of assets using different market instruments, in an effort to identify business opportunities and quantify business risks. The Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team maintains its independent view of North American wholesale power markets in its bi-annual Reference Case.

Responsibilities of a Managing Consultant include, but are not limited to, the following:
- Originating, closing, leading large and complex client engagements.

- Managing staff and assisting in related business development efforts.

- Tracking and analyzing energy market trends.

- Translating clients' inquiries and challenges into actionable scopes of work.

- Compiling reports, presentations, and other documents to communicate solutions, strategies, and analysis to clients.

- Supporting the day-to-day management of client relationships.

- Developing and using analytical models, programming, and simulations to forecast market prices, conduct research and development, and create tools to improve productivity and accuracy.

- Reviewing and approving model outputs via data collection, manipulation, and analyses, which may involve spreadsheet and database creation and management.

On our team you’ll:
- Be an expert in ISO/RTO markets across North America, at the crossroads of local energy pricing, capacity auctions, ancillary services and shifts in load composition and demand response initiatives

- Be intimately familiar with the economics, policies and players driving renewables, battery storage development, green fuels and new power generation technologies.

- Supervise simulations of the future dispatch of the power transmission grid using an economic dispatch model.

- Review the addition/retirement of diverse generating resources using a capacity expansion model across ISO/RTO markets.

- Be an expert in how energy players procure power, integrate renewables, and maintain grid reliability.

- Help develop our Reference Case while expanding our client base.

- Mentor junior consultants in expanding their individual know-how and business acumen on energy markets, business development and client management skills.

What You Will Need :
- Must be a US Citizen or US Permanent Resident due to nature of client engagements.

- Bachelor’s degree in a business, economics, energy finance, or engineering discipline AND Five (5+) plus years of post-graduation work experience in a related field (e.g. consulting, strategy, project development); Or  Master's degree in a business, economics, energy finance, or engineering discipline AND Three (3+) plus years of post-graduation work experience in a related field (e.g. consulting, strategy, project development).

- Post graduation work experience with economic dispatch models such as: Aurora, Origin, PLEXOS, BID3, or PSO.

- Outstanding analytical and problem-solving skills.

- Experienced with data analytics, data modeling and visualization.

- Proactive and independent work style.

- Ability to assume ownership of significant portions of tasks while collaborating with a close-knit team.

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

- Ability to travel.

- Ability to work in a Guidehouse Office or Client Office location.

- Currently reside in the contiguous United States.

What Would Be Nice To Have :
- Preference will be given to candidates within reasonable driving distance of a core Guidehouse Office or Client Office location.

- Graduate degree (Masters, MBA, PhD) in business, policy, economics, energy finance, engineering.

- Experience in generation and storage asset management.

The annual salary range for this position is $130,000.00-$216,000.00. Compensation decisions depend on a wide range of factors, including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, security clearances, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs.

jobs.description:

What You Will Do:
Guidehouse’s Health Technology Consulting team helps healthcare organizations improve clinical operations, financial performance, patient experience, and workforce effectiveness through better use of enterprise technology. Our EHR practice supports health systems across strategy, implementation, optimization, adoption, and value realization.
The Managing Consultant will lead Epic patient flow and capacity management engagements for hospitals and health systems. This role requires deep knowledge of Epic Grand Central and the operational processes that govern patient placement, transfers, bed management, environmental services, transport, discharge progression, and enterprise capacity management.
The Managing Consultant will work directly with hospital executives, operational leaders, clinicians, informatics teams, and application teams to design practical solutions that improve throughput and the use of available capacity. The individual must be able to connect operational policy, staffing models, governance, workflows, Epic configuration, reporting, and adoption.

- Lead Epic Grand Central implementation, optimization, assessment, and stabilization engagements.

- Assess current patient flow operations, system configuration, decision rights, performance data, and organizational constraints.

- Design future-state workflows for bed requests, bed assignment, patient placement, transfers, level-of-care changes, environmental services, patient transport, discharge progression, and capacity escalation.

- Advise clients on centralized and decentralized patient placement models, transfer center operations, bed management responsibilities, escalation pathways, and capacity governance.

- Support the design or optimization of capacity command centers, including operating models, roles, decision authority, escalation thresholds, communication processes, technology, and performance measures.

- Lead the design and validation of Epic Grand Central functionality, including patient movement, bed planning, bed boards, unit and room configuration, transfer workflows, environmental services, transport, discharge status, and related operational tools.

- Evaluate dependencies across Epic Grand Central, Prelude, Cadence, ASAP, EpicCare Inpatient, OpTime, Rover, Cogito, reporting tools, interfaces, and third-party capacity management solutions.

- Translate operational requirements into system design decisions, build specifications, workflow documentation, testing scenarios, and implementation plans.

- Lead integrated testing, workflow validation, clinical and operational simulations, cutover planning, training readiness, go-live support, and post-live stabilization.

- Develop recommendations to reduce avoidable patient delays, emergency department boarding, transfer friction, bed turnaround time, and unnecessary variation in patient placement.

- Establish performance measures and reporting requirements related to occupancy, throughput, length of stay, discharge progression, bed turnaround, transport response, transfer acceptance, and capacity constraints.

- Facilitate working sessions with nursing, hospital operations, transfer center, environmental services, transport, emergency department, procedural, ancillary, and technology leaders.

- Communicate findings, risks, recommendations, and decisions to senior client leaders in a clear and direct manner.

- Manage project scope, workplans, deliverables, risks, issues, dependencies, timelines, and team assignments.

- Lead and develop consultants and client team members through structured coaching, review, and feedback.

- Support proposal development, solution design, level-of-effort estimates, presentations, and other practice development activities.

- Develop reusable methods, tools, assessments, and points of view for the Guidehouse EHR practice.

- Ability to travel up to 50% based on client and project requirements.

What You Will Need:
- Bachelor’s degree obtained from an accredited college or university.

- Minimum of five years of relevant experience in EHR implementation, optimization, healthcare technology, patient flow operations, or a related field.

- Epic Grand Central certification or prior certification with the ability to obtain or renew certification within an agreed period.

- Demonstrated experience leading Epic Grand Central implementation, optimization, upgrade, stabilization, or operational improvement work.

- Strong understanding of hospital patient flow, bed management, transfers, environmental services, patient transport, discharge progression, and capacity management.

- Experience leading project teams, application teams, operational workgroups, or major project workstreams.

- Experience developing and managing project plans, deliverables, risks, issues, dependencies, and client decisions.

- Ability to facilitate complex discussions involving operational, clinical, technical, and executive stakeholders.

- Ability to convert operational problems into clear workflow, technology, governance, and measurement recommendations.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting recommendations to senior leaders.

- Consulting experience or significant client-facing experience in a healthcare organization, EHR vendor, or healthcare technology environment.

- Ability to travel up to 50% based on client and project requirements.

- Ability to support major implementation and go-live activities, which may occasionally occur outside standard business hours.

- Additional Epic certification or experience in Prelude, Cadence, ASAP, EpicCare Inpatient, OpTime, Rover, Cogito, or related applications.

- Experience with transfer centers, centralized patient placement, enterprise bed management, or multi-hospital capacity coordination.

What You Will Do:

We are looking for a Managing Consultant to join our Life Sciences team, which supports pharmaceutical and biotech companies with commercial insights and strategy as well as data and business analytics. This role will be a primary member of our Life Science advisory team, and collaborate closely with our firmwide Data, Advanced Analytics, and Technology Transformation teams to shape the growth of our Life Science data services offerings.

Candidates should be market-facing self-starters who take ownership of their work, are enthusiastic, and have a collaborative mindset to support our efforts to sell and provide consulting solutions. You will coordinate activities across multiple projects and provide experience-based insight across strategy, commercial analytics, and data-driven solution design.

As a Life Science Managing Consultant, you will:
- Translate client's key business questions and structuring/executing comprehensive analytics plans to provide necessary insights (e.g., cross-sectional analyses, longitudinal studies, inferential statistics, and structured decision support).
- Convey and summarize detailed data insights through a strategic lens that is understandable and actionable by cross-functional internal/external stakeholders.
- Leverage various commercial and real-world evidence datasets to drive insights that address client business problems, which include but are not limited to medical and pharmacy claims (open and closed), formulary and managed care data, and EMR data.

- Work with strategy consulting teams and data science teams to design and execute data-driven projects, such as market sizing/segmentation, patient journey, provider profiling/targeting, provider affiliation mapping, epidemiology studies, managed care analytics, pull-through modeling/program design, forecasting, field force design, KPI/performance tracking, and incentive comp.

- Support managing contract budgets, developing and sharing best practices, and evolving Guidehouse’s data and analytics capabilities.

What You Will Need:
- Bachelor's Degree; FOUR (4) years of additional professional experience in lieu of Bachelor's
- FOUR (4+) years of Life Sciences industry, management consulting, and/or data vendor experience is required, plus advanced degree MBA, PhD, PharmD or MD.
- Experience in commercial management consulting functions such as portfolio and asset strategy, data/commercial analytics, launch excellence & brand planning, patient services and market access is a plus.
- Must possess strong analytical skills (Excel, Access, etc.) and leverage analytic techniques to use data to guide client and team decision-making.
- Must have advanced data collection, research, and information-finding experience and explore solutions that challenge critical thinking.
- 3+ years of experience in business & data analytics.
- Experience with sophisticated drug forecasting techniques.
- Must be willing to travel to client sites across the US up to 20% of the time.
- Authorized to work for any US employer without sponsorship.

- Advanced degree, MBA, Information Systems, Healthcare Management, Innovation and entrepreneurship, or similar quantitative discipline.
- In-line and pipeline forecasting and NPV modeling.
- Technical/product management and software experience.
- Experience with common analytic toolsets such as SQL, R, Python, Snowflake.
- Proficiency in data visualization services such as PowerBI, Tableau.
- Ability to build client-ready forecast models/ financial models.
- Ability to work with large data sets such as claims data.
- Excellent attention to detail and ability to review work products of self and others and produce work products and deliverables that require minimal re-work or editing.

What You Will Do :

Support Federal clients across the full spectrum of financial management, including federal grants, reimbursable agreements, procurement processes, and budget formulation and execution. This role requires strong client relationship and presentation skills, analytical skills, knowledge of Federal financial management regulations and processes, and the ability to translate complex financial data into clear insights and recommendations for clients. Works as part of a cross-functional team to deliver high-quality work products on time and in alignment with client goals.

Financial Management & Analysis:
- Provide ongoing financial management support to Federal clients in accordance with applicable Federal financial management requirements and guidance.

- Support the quantitative development of business case documentation (for example, needs analyses and cost/benefit analyses).

- Prepare, review, and reconcile financial documents such as federal financial transaction data, reimbursable agreements, and grant related financial records.

- Identify opportunities for process improvement and propose practical recommendations to enhance financial operations and controls.

Client Delivery & Communication:
- Develop clear, well-structured deliverables (presentations, reports, analyses, dashboards) that synthesize complex financial information into actionable insights and recommendations for clients, including visually appealing, high-level summaries of large financial datasets for various levels of stakeholders.

- Facilitate client meetings and working sessions to gather data, understand requirements, and validate findings.

- Communicate with client and internal stakeholders on project status, findings, and next steps, including explaining financial concepts to non-financial audiences and summarizing key takeaways from external and internal stakeholder meetings.

- Provide analysis and insight to managers and leadership to inform decision-making and project direction.

Innovation & Problem Solving:
- Perform research and analysis to identify and obtain needed information, including applicable Federal regulations, policies, best practices, and public financial data sources such as USASpending.gov to investigate financial transaction-level discrepancies.

- Address issues and problems that are generally defined and may involve multiple interrelated factors, applying sound judgment within established frameworks and guidance.

- Recommend changes to processes, tools, or documentation to solve problems and improve efficiency or compliance, including documenting current data analysis processes, identifying improvement opportunities, and iterating on data displays or communication methods to advance PMO goals.

- Work as part of a team or independently while taking ownership of assigned tasks and workstreams, proactively brainstorming path-forward options and asking targeted questions when guidance is needed.

- Assist on large to mid-sized, moderately complex projects or task orders, including coordinating specific activities or deliverables.

What You Will Do :
A career within Guidehouse Health will provide you with the opportunity to help clients transform care delivery, technology, and operations through large-scale modernization initiatives. We partner with federal agencies and healthcare organizations to drive organizational change, accelerate adoption, and ensure stakeholders are prepared to successfully navigate evolving business processes, technologies, and ways of working.
Our Strategic Change Communications Consultants help clients translate complex transformation efforts into actionable, audience-centered communications that build awareness, understanding, readiness, and adoption. Working closely with executives, program leadership, technical teams, and operational stakeholders, you will develop strategic communications that support workforce transformation, organizational readiness, and successful implementation of modernization initiatives.
Specific responsibilities include:
Strategic Change Communications and Adoption
- Develop and execute integrated change communication strategies that support large-scale modernization, transformation, and technology implementation efforts.

- Design communications approaches that increase awareness, stakeholder readiness, user adoption, and sustained behavioral change.

- Assess stakeholder impacts and communication needs across multiple audiences, tailoring messaging to address varying levels of technical knowledge, organizational influence, and change readiness.

- Partner with change management, training, technical, and business teams to align communications with implementation milestones and organizational readiness objectives.

- Develop communication plans that include stakeholder analysis, audience segmentation, key messages, communication channels, feedback mechanisms, risks, and success measures.

Executive Communications and Strategic Advisory Support
- Serve as a trusted communications advisor to executive leaders, helping translate strategic priorities, decisions, and transformation objectives into impactful communications.

- Develop executive-level products, including leadership messages, talking points, presentations, briefing materials, leadership toolkits, and stakeholder engagement materials.

- Role changes and workforce impacts

- Benefits realization and organizational outcomes

- Facilitate communication planning sessions, stakeholder workshops, leadership briefings, and readiness discussions.

jobs.title: Emergency Management Partnerships, Engagement, and Strategy Senior Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Family :
Strategy & Transformation Consulting
Travel Required :
Up to 10%
Clearance Required :
Ability to Obtain Public Trust

What You Will Do :
Serve as the Partnerships, Engagement, and Strategy Senior Consultant supporting FEMA's mission to help people before, during, and after disasters. As a Guidehouse Senior Consultant embedded within an operational office of the U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), you will leverage your emergency management experience to strengthen FEMA's relationships with state, local, tribal, and territorial governments, private sector organizations, nongovernmental organizations, and other key stakeholders that play a critical role in disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience.

In this role, you will lead communications, engagement, and partnership initiatives designed to foster collaboration, enhance information sharing, and improve coordination between FEMA and external partners. You will build and sustain trusted relationships across critical infrastructure sectors and private industry, helping FEMA identify emerging risks, strengthen preparedness efforts, and maintain situational awareness before, during, and after disasters.
You will develop and execute stakeholder engagement strategies, facilitate meetings and workshops, prepare executive-level communications and briefing materials, and translate complex operational and analytical information into clear, actionable recommendations. You will also support FEMA leadership in identifying opportunities to expand partnerships, increase stakeholder participation, and advance initiatives that strengthen community resilience nationwide.

This position is ideal for an individual with a passion for emergency management, relationship-building, strategic communications, and public service. Success in this role requires the ability to engage diverse stakeholders, navigate complex operational environments, and develop collaborative solutions that help FEMA and its partners better serve disaster survivors and strengthen the nation's resilience.

This position is embedded within FEMA Headquarters in Washington, D.C., and requires an onsite presence of approximately four (4) days per week at the client site. Team members are also expected to spend approximately one (1) day per week at Guidehouse's Tysons, VA or Arlington, VA office to support collaboration, leadership engagement, and professional development activities.

Duties will include:
- Lead the development, execution, and management of partnerships, engagement, and strategic communication initiatives that strengthen collaboration between FEMA, government partners, nongovernmental organizations, private sector organizations, and critical infrastructure stakeholders.

- Build and sustain trusted relationships with external partners to advance disaster preparedness, response, recovery, mitigation, and resilience objectives.

- Develop and implement engagement strategies, outreach plans, and communications campaigns that promote FEMA programs, initiatives, and partnership opportunities.

- Research, analyze, and communicate emerging risks, operational challenges, disaster impacts, and resilience initiatives to inform situational awareness and stakeholder decision-making.

- Facilitate coordination among federal, state, local, tribal, territorial, nonprofit, and private-sector partners to support information sharing and collaborative problem-solving.

- Plan. develop, and manage multi‑channel communications and content with minimal oversight; create/develop plain‑language messaging, graphics, and content to increase stakeholder engagement.

- Develop executive-level briefings, talking points, reports, presentations, and other communications products that clearly translate complex operational and analytical information into evidence-based recommendations for FEMA leadership and external stakeholders.

- Research and communicate supply chain logistics, impacts, disruptors, and resilience efforts across the disaster lifecycle to inform business operations and customers.

- Conduct market research, stakeholder analysis, and environmental scans to identify partnership opportunities, emerging trends, and engagement strategies that advance FEMA mission priorities.

- Plan, organize, and facilitate client meetings, workshops, exercises, and stakeholder engagements involving senior leaders, external partners, and disaster management professionals.

- Define, track, analyze, and report communications, engagement, and partnership performance metrics, including return-on-investment (ROI) measures; analyze results and evaluate effectiveness and inform continuous improvement efforts.

- Apply qualitative and quantitative analysis to assess stakeholder needs, identify gaps, and support the development of evidence-based engagement and resilience strategies.

- Support FEMA leadership in identifying opportunities to expand partnerships, strengthen cross-sector collaboration, and increase stakeholder participation in preparedness and resilience initiatives.

- Deliver high-quality client service and project execution in a dynamic, fast-paced emergency management environment, independently managing priorities, deadlines, and deliverables.

- Mentor junior team members, provide quality assurance for project work products, and contribute to a collaborative, mission-focused team environment.

- Demonstrate initiative, strategic thinking, and creative problem-solving to address complex emergency management challenges and improve client outcomes.

What You Will Need:
- Must be able to OBTAIN and MAINTAIN a Federal or DoD "PUBLIC TRUST"; candidates must obtain approved adjudication of their PUBLIC TRUST prior to onboarding with Guidehouse. Candidates with an ACTIVE PUBLIC TRUST or SUITABILITY are preferred.
- Bachelor's degree.

- SIX (6) years of experience in emergency management or a closely related field. Knowledge of the following:

- Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)

- National Response Coordination Center (NRCC) structure

- DHS Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)

- National Response and Recovery Framework (NRF) and (NDRF) respectively

- How private sector and industry integrates with the federal government.

- Experience in communications, customer experience, partner engagement, marketing, or training.

- Experience leading end‑to‑end work products; collaborating across stakeholders to collect input, adjudicate feedback, and deliver on time.

- Experience modernizing or redesigning communications products to meet evolving business requirements.

- Experience developing and executing partnership engagement strategies with minimal errors and oversight in fast‑paced environments.

What Would Be Nice To Have :
- Candidates with an ACTIVE PUBLIC TRUST or SUITABILITY are preferred

- Strong oral and written communication skills for diverse audiences; demonstrated ability to communicate in plain language.

- Experience planning, executing, and facilitating meetings, summits, and conferences (in‑person, online, and hybrid) to drive outcomes and consensus with internal and client stakeholders.

- Experience presenting and facilitating using collaboration tools and feedback technologies.

- Successful experience briefing senior executives and developing communication strategies tailored to client needs.

- Experience developing executive talking points and presentation materials.

- Proven ability to manage own work.

- Federal consulting and/or Federal Government experience, preferably supporting FEMA, DHS, emergency management, homeland security, or resilience programs.

- Familiarity with how private sector and industry integrates with the federal government.

- Experience supporting emergency management, disaster preparedness, response, recovery, mitigation, resilience, or public-private partnership initiatives.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Suite applications

- Demonstrated experience building and sustaining relationships with government, nonprofit, private-sector, and critical infrastructure stakeholders.

- Experience conducting market research, stakeholder analysis, and environmental scans to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and partnership strategies.

- Crisis communications, business continuity, or incident management communications experience.

- Strong project management, relationship-building, analytical, and problem-solving skills in a fast-paced environment.

jobs.title: Healthcare Partner, Managed Care Consulting
jobs.description:
Job Family :
Strategy & Transformation Consulting
Travel Required :
Up to 50%
Clearance Required :
None

What You Will Do:

The desired Partner, Managed Care Advisory will have the opportunity to drive significant revenue enhancement and strategic repositioning for healthcare clients. This leader will be responsible for helping organizations identify and capture millions in potential revenue through comprehensive managed care solutions, including commercial rate benchmarking and payer price transparency analytics. The role involves navigating complex contract negotiations, particularly with challenging payers, and developing strategies that can transform a client's financial performance. This leader’s impact will extend beyond immediate financial gains, potentially helping distressed healthcare organizations improve their margin and market positioning by addressing critical managed care contract challenges.

The Partner, Managed Care Consulting is a senior leadership position within the Guidehouse Healthcare Practice, specifically focused on leading and driving growth for the Healthcare sector. This partner will be responsible for bringing and developing a book of business and have an oversight of ongoing project delivery solution development and management of teams across multiple concurrent client engagements across our managed care vertical. This role is critical to the success of the overall practice growth strategy, and will have responsibility for originating, closing, and managing clients, leading consulting teams, and ensuring the delivery of high-quality revenue cycle strategies and programs. This leader must be both strategic and operational, possessing deep knowledge and experience on how health systems work. They must successfully develop and execute against the vision for Managed Care services, including driving consulting projects that outline transformative initiatives to contain costs, enhance revenues, and lay out initiatives for execution across the firm for impact. Tying these initiatives to metrics and KPIs to show both revenue increases and cost containment success is crucial to the role. They must be experts in selling and delivering advisory work that assists healthcare organizations in optimizing performance, enhancing efficiency and ensuring compliance within industry regulations. This role is key in shaping and driving consulting opportunities across the entire managed care life cycle. This Partner will be key in helping build out the Managed Care practice, helping develop and mentor consultants in new methods to enhance performance improvement and drive impactful transformation initiatives leveraging the Guidehouse platform.

The ideal candidate will co-lead the managed care practice that has the strong analytical staff, benchmarking and price transparency processes, as well as the reputation in the managed care place to advance the practice and work alongside highly experienced industry leaders to make meaningful change for clients served across 150+ markets.

Primarily the responsibilities for this role include:
- Drive revenue enhancement, risk mitigation, and strategic repositioning for healthcare clients, with a focus on improving revenue and margins

- Manage the full managed care contracting cycle, including analytics, strategy preparation, negotiations, and post-contract implementation

- Develop and execute comprehensive managed care solutions, including commercial rate benchmarking, payer price transparency analytics, and contract negotiations

- Bring new clients to the table, with a partner-level revenue target of $8 million or higher

- Provide strategic insights across the healthcare ecosystem, including working with C-suite executives to transform revenue and market positioning

- Lead business development of advisory pursuits within the territory/market.
- Activities include originating new consulting opportunities, driving assessments in the front end, current v. future state performance, expanding and extending current advisory engagements, relationship-based selling to new clients, leading RFP responses, and representing the firm at business development-related conferences

- Lead advisory and delivery teams on high-impact revenue cycle transformation client engagements within territory/market.
- Activities include: client relationship management, consulting delivery execution, project financial management, risk/quality management, and client satisfaction management

- Build a book of business through senior client relationship management by finding, closing and delivering Managed Care growth initiatives

- Manage teams consisting of consulting experts and advisory personnel to cover key accounts

- Responsible for contract growth, and uncovering and assisting in originating and capturing new opportunities that land and expand revenue cycle programs with clients

- Manage transaction deals sizes ranging from $500K to multi-million dollars annually with pull through to managed services that are multi year

- This role will also support the Next Gen Payer-Provider healthcare horizontal joint initiatives between the managed care and the payer practice

- Key to this role will be able to cross sell other guide house services to broaden accounts and exposure in the marketplace parentheses (e.g. access performance excellence, strategy digital etc)/

- Provide expertise and deep experience in Managed Care to evolve deal constructs, teaming opportunities, and portfolio evolution

- Lead client management and growth in Managed Care by leveraging design, development, and implementation skills to advise and guide clients to best options

- Interface, manage, and expand relationships with client CEOs, CFOs, CTOs and other senior executives to demonstrate how solutions set the strategy for enhancing operational efficiency, financial health, and patient care quality.

- Own and build critical business and industry relationships, both internally and externally

- Advise clients based on knowledge of operations best practices, industry trends, market happenings, and the newest technology innovations

- Team and collaborate across the firm to drive maximum value for clients

What You Will Need:
- Previous executive consulting or industry leadership with Medicaid OR Medicare/Medicare Advantage (STARS and quality), accountable care organization, or patient centered medical home highly desirable

- 15+ years professional experience in a combination of the following:
- ACO leadership

- Managed care

- Health Plan or Payer leadership

- Health Plan executive level contract management

- IT/Data management

- Quality management

- Client-facing healthcare consulting role

- Health policy analysis and health economics research.

- Risk predication and adjustment methods, and performance-based procurement,

- Quality and total cost measures of care for Federal, State, and health plans who participate in the Affordable Care Act, Medicaid, and Medicare programs.

- Superb problem-solving and interpersonal skills Demonstrated use of analytical skills that found innovative, holistic, value based strategic solutions

- Demonstrated ability to lead and supervise staff in a collaborative and matrixed team environment to achieve budget and timeline goals

- Ability to sell consulting and building strong client relationships at the executive level, demonstrated by persuading boards and C-suites of Government Health State Agencies, Health Plan and Payor organizations to action

- Bachelor's degree from accredited school required

- Demonstrated leadership achieving outcomes in healthcare consulting focused strategy and transformation projects

- Proven verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to persuade senior management or Knowledge of Medicaid managed care operational program elements including MMIS, eligibility and enrollment, captivation payments, quality performance and care coordination

- Travel up to 50% as the job requires

What Be Nice to Have :

Sales and Commercial Excellence
- Demonstrated experience in selling Managed Care contracts for projects that support large hospital systems and physician organizations, as well as community hospitals, academic medical centers, and mid to large-size regional healthcare providers.

- Deep experience originating front end deals and getting new logos by positioning best practices, industry trends and leveraging existing relationships and developing new ones

- A consulting sales leader that is constantly scouring for new opportunities, leveraging their experience and relationships in the managed care space to sell assessments and shape consulting deals for the entire Managed Care life cycle (strategy, technology, operations, etc)

- A demonstrated sales record of consistent achievement of $8-10 million+ annually within Healthcare Managed Care Advisory and skills, relationships and market knowledge to build a book of business quickly

- Player/Coach that drives all client facing and business development activities for selling advisory and positioning digital and managed services end to end projects.
Leverages strategy, financial and operational knowledge to serve as a consulting leader to sell advisory to healthcare executives using learned experiences and best practices, the latest industry trends, regulation changes, and market movements to compel them to act.

- Utilize proper sales operations discipline (e.g. pipeline analytics, offering collaterals, tracking scorecards) to performance manage the team

- Can coach strategy consultants on best practices for developing and growing executive client relationships

- Can create a high-energy environment among the consulting team that drives enthusiasm, optimism, and a relentless focus on solving client problems, winning deals, and achieving performance metrics

- Can originate opportunities, oversee sales and delivery, and engage in closing entry point projects to position land and expand opportunities across the revenue cycle continuum.

Managed Care Domain Knowledge
- Deep payer strategy and advisory experience in the drivers that can enhance optimizing operations, financial health, and patient outcomes while navigating complex regulatory environments

- A deep experience developing and executing negotiation strategies for provider and payer healthcare clients to improve their financial posture from both a revenue enhancement and cost containment perspective

- Deep experience in either industry and/or consulting driving optimization work, including analytics around benchmarking to help inform fact-based negotiation strategy and positions

- Negotiation experience from strategy through execution in the healthcare ecosystem internally and externally including partners to make improvements

- Experience in CDM optimization, revenue rebalancing, managed care benchmarking, price transparency, strategic pricing, managed care strategy, contract language review and automated analytics platform for benchmarking type services will be crucial.

- A deep understanding across the healthcare system environment to lay out roadmaps for broad transformations and restructuring work to sell discrete projects that satisfy strategic goals

- An expert in areas such as EBITDA improvement, turnarounds, tech innovation, operating model redesign, financial performance, and foundational processes in a healthcare system.

- Deep understanding of industry trends towards greater price transparency and the technology enabled solutions to support an evolving marketplace as well as other analytical advancements that impact clients

- Deep strategic consulting in large scale transformations that impact operational performance and implement technology transformations and strategic planning

- Experience partnering with healthcare systems, hospitals, physician organizations, and multi-site healthcare entities, reinforced by a deep knowledge of key players in the market

- Ability to tailor solutions that address the unique challenges of the healthcare industry driving performance and patient outcomes

Delivery Excellence
- Track record of advising clients on payer revenue and contract yield leading practices, clinical operations, technology strategy, and innovative care, leveraging deep industry insights to drive performance improvement to ensure its proper delivery.

- Demonstrated experience in developing strategic roadmaps and ensuring consulting teams deliver the plans to drive financial and operational performance improvements that help organizations streamline processes, reduce costs, and enhance efficiency.

- The ideal candidate will come with a reputation for selling and delivering Managed Care transformations that made an everlasting impact to healthcare clients and can be replicated Deep experience in creating compelling deliverables and work products that clients have used to drive performance improvement initiatives with impact.

- Ideal candidates will have a record of relationship building, selling and delivering roadmaps of work, strong employee and team satisfaction metrics, focusing on an employee experience focused management approach

- Ability to manage multiple pursuits and overseeing and coaching teams on internal operations and methodologies for effective programs.

- Proven ability to sell and deliver across the entire Guidehouse portfolio

- Focused on Managed Care and ensuring projects are delivered on time and on budget

- Can leverage delivery insights into addressing problems before they happen and looking for cross-sell opportunities

Client Management
- Has C-Level relationships and can build others with senior executives at healthcare entities, including Partners, to serve with excellence and quality

- Develops account planning programs for proper client coverage to go deep and wide (expand the “pipe and pie”) in serving clients holistically

- Brings clients new ideas based on the market, industry and technology trends proactively to keep them ahead of achieving their goals

- Bring strong provider and payer market relationships with senior executives and be able to gain traction rapidly on selling new business

- Ideal candidates will lead with empathy and have an extensive set of relationships, capabilities, and approaches to bring firm offerings to client needs in an authentic, mission-driven, and client service-focused manner

- Track record of building and expanding client partnerships through the development and delivery of new advisory services solutions

- Ability to build new processes and solutions to improve client satisfaction, service quality and market penetration

Scale & Execution
- Experience selling a roadmap of managed care services that start with consulting and advisory to position larger deals across the Guidehouse portfolio

- Demonstrated experience selling and delivering large, concurrent consulting projects that made impact and delivered results to replicate at other healthcare organizations.

- Track record of consistent achievement of building and growing a book of business of $8-$10 million annually within healthcare Managed Care

- Disciplined operator who performance-manages their consulting team with rigor and discipline and develops best practices and processes for constant improvement

- A KPI-driven leader that monitors the health of the business and takes proactive action for improvements and innovation

Culture Fit & Leadership
- A strategic thought leader, expert in Managed Care advisory, driven to improve financial and operational improvement in healthcare.

- Personable, humble, confident and experienced proactive leader able to function in a matrix

- Charismatic visionary with high EQ, high IQ, and low ego

- A strong leader and communicator able to guide and mentor their team to successful outcomes

- A resilient consulting expert who has the proven experience to work through client opportunities and issues to get results, improve ways of working, and deliver quality results
Demonstrated experience grooming the following generations of leadership

- Proven experience building and transforming teams, driving service and quality excellence

- Ability to articulate mature hiring and management philosophies as well as leading best practice methodology development to improve overall consulting performance.

- Ability to navigate and lead through ambiguity

- Highly credible, leadership polish, and winning instincts

- Collaborative team player that works well to best serve clients and Guidehouse across the firm

Personal characteristics

The ideal candidate must possess strong people skills and the ability to function effectively in a matrix management environment. They should be adaptable, capable of working across different organizational structures, and not rigidly hierarchical. The leader must have excellent interpersonal abilities who can lead and develop team members. They must have high emotional intelligence who can collaborate effectively. Some important details include:
- Strategically minded, operationally inclined, and action-oriented

- Market facing deal maker and delivery/operational leader

jobs.description:

Is life sciences in your DNA? Breakthroughs in pharma are helping people live healthier lives, while medical devices enable patients to proactively maintain health – this is undoubtedly a transformative time for health care companies. Guidehouse’s Life Sciences practice is an engine of innovation, helping pharmaceutical, biotech, medical device, and diagnostic companies develop custom solutions that tackle today’s challenges, while anticipating tomorrows. You will have an immediate impact by partnering with our clients, across all levels, to deliver product planning, pricing, reimbursement, product commercialization, and regulatory and compliance solutions. Do you think you are up for the challenge?

We continuously strive to foster an inclusive and diverse work culture and thoughtfully develop our people through challenging work, valuable learning and educational programs. We cultivate a culture of mentorship and feedback for professional and personal growth. We help our clients take control of their future. This mission extends to our employee's careers, health and well-being and by the many ways we give back to our communities.

What You Will Do :
The Value & Access team provides commercialization strategy and market access services to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies. Our client services range from pre-commercialization go-to-market planning to launch value story, pricing, and reimbursement strategies, impacting policies affecting the use and payment of our clients’ novel therapies.

You will be responsible for creating and implementing pricing and access strategies for a variety of pharmaceutical assets. This will involve working with senior staff to develop project proposals, managing consulting teams in the development and communication of client deliverables, and maintaining client relationships. Managing Consultants oversee multiple projects simultaneously.

Common responsibilities and expertise include:
·      Designing and managing project teams to execute various pharmaceutical market access and pricing strategy projects, both qualitative and quantitative
○     Strong market analysis, market research, and analytics skills required
○     Preferred candidates will have experience with various pricing methodologies (analog assessment, Van Westendorp, Gabor Granger, Conjoint, etc.)
·      Designing and leading primary interviews with key stakeholders such as payers and KOLs
·      Deep experience with:
- Part A / hospital inpatient pricing and reimbursement

- Part B / medical benefit pricing

- Part D / contracting

- Calculating gross-to-net

·      Building Excel-based financial models to evaluate price-access scenarios and gross-to-net
·      Strong understanding of health economic methodologies and value pricing constructs
·      Ability to construct practice economic analyses under a variety of settings of care and financial ecosystems
·      Familiarity with U.S. government and pricing policy reform
·      Track record of thought leadership (written or podium)
·      Comfortable engaging with and presenting to executive-level audiences to deliver actionable insights and recommendations
·      Track record of training and developing junior consulting staff

Guidehouse encourages career development and hiring for the long term.  Managing Consultants follow a clearly defined career path. As Managing Consultants hone their project management skills, ability to manage multiple work streams, professional expertise, and client and business development skills, they progress to the position of Associate Director.

What You Will Need :
·      Bachelor’s degree; a major course of study in science, biomedical engineering, business, or healthcare policy preferred.
·      4+ years of consulting or related business experience in market access, reimbursement, pricing, health economics, forecasting, and/or pipeline strategy.
·      1–2 years of direct experience in client management and content delivery roles.
·      Demonstrates excellent project management skills, initiative and resourcefulness, leadership, and ability to think strategically and creatively.
·      Keen attention to detail.
·      Strong understanding of the pharmaceutical industry, including drug development and launch.

·      Strong verbal and written communication skills.
·      Proficiency in Microsoft Office Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

We are seeking an experienced AI and data practitioner to join our growing AI and Data practice with a dedicated focus on State Health agencies, with an emphasis on Medicaid programs and the responsible development and operationalization of AI solutions. This individual will be a hands-on leader who can connect strategy to execution, partnering with agency leaders to define high-value AI use cases, establish an enterprise AI strategy, and advance AI enablement across the organization.
This is a leadership role for someone who thrives at the intersection of state health mission outcomes, data and AI capabilities, and practical implementation. You will guide clients through the full lifecycle, from identifying and prioritizing use cases to designing the operating model, data foundations, governance, and delivery approach needed to move solutions into production.
The Associate Director will oversee cross-functional teams and work directly with client executives and program leaders to drive measurable value through AI, analytics, and modern data practices.

Key Responsibilities Include

Client Leadership and Delivery
- Serve as a trusted advisor to State Health and Medicaid leaders on developing an AI strategy that covers: - Core enterprise AI capabilities (data readiness, governance, model lifecycle management, tooling)
- Priority mission and operational use cases (member and provider experience, program operations, integrity, quality, and analytics)

- Lead engagements from strategy through implementation, with a focus on outcomes, adoption, and sustainable operations.
- Translate complex health and Medicaid business challenges into actionable AI/ML and analytics solutions using platforms such as Azure, AWS, GCP, Databricks, Snowflake, and related services.
- Partner with IT, program, privacy, security, legal, and procurement stakeholders to support delivery that aligns to agency policies and applicable regulations.

AI Strategy, Use Case Portfolio, and Roadmaps
- Facilitate use case discovery and prioritization workshops with stakeholders across agency divisions.
- Define an AI use case portfolio and roadmap that balances: - Quick-win productivity use cases
- Program modernization and longer-term transformation
- Foundational capabilities (data, governance, operating model) needed to scale

- Intelligent document processing, summarization, and search
- Customer service and contact center augmentation
- Caseworker support tools and workflow automation
- Program integrity and anomaly detection

- Partner with data engineering and architecture teams to design data pipelines and curated datasets that support trusted analytics and AI use.

- Collaborate with security and privacy stakeholders to align to expectations relevant to State Health environments (for example, HIPAA-aligned privacy practices, agency security controls, and contractual requirements).

- Strong understanding of AI/ML technologies and data platforms (for example Azure/AWS/GCP, Databricks, Snowflake), and modern analytics methodologies.

jobs.description:

Up to 25%

What You Will Do:

The Head of Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) will lead enterprise-wide financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, and strategic decision support for a complex professional services organization serving both federal and commercial markets. This highly visible leader will partner with the Chief Financial Officer, executive leadership, segment leaders, and functional stakeholders to translate business performance into actionable insights, strengthen financial discipline, and support profitable growth.

The Head of FP&A will build and lead a high-performing team, establish scalable planning and reporting processes, and provide forward-looking analysis across revenue, backlog, pipeline, labor, utilization, indirect costs, margins, cash flow, and capital allocation. The successful candidate will bring strong professional services experience, fluency in both federal contracting and commercial business models, and the energy, collaboration skills, and performance orientation required to influence leaders across the organization. An appetite to innovate and leverage modern means and methods to accomplish desired outcomes is critical.   The ability to simultaneously manage the details and understand the big picture is a key requirement for success in the role.  Experience leading the function in a publicly traded company is required.  Guidehouse is seeking a high-energy, hardworking leader who is deeply committed to and passionate about our mission, approaches colleagues and clients with humility and integrity, and thrives in a collaborative environment.

Key Responsibilities:

- Lead the company’s annual budgeting, quarterly forecasting, monthly outlook, and long-range planning processes across federal, commercial, corporate, and shared-service operations.
- Own executive, Board, and management reporting, delivering clear analysis of financial results, key performance drivers, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
- Partner with segment and functional leaders to translate operational plans, sales pipeline, backlog, staffing, utilization, pricing, and investment decisions into integrated financial forecasts.
- Provide strategic financial modeling, scenario analysis, and decision support for growth initiatives, acquisitions, integrations, investments, and cost optimization opportunities.
- Strengthen forecasting accuracy and accountability through driver-based planning, disciplined variance analysis, and consistent performance metrics.
- Oversee financial analysis for federal government contracting, including revenue recognition, indirect rates, project economics, backlog, funded and unfunded work, and relevant compliance considerations.
- Develop reporting and insights for commercial professional services operations, including bookings, pipeline conversion, pricing, utilization, realization, revenue, margin, and client profitability.
- Collaborate closely with Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Corporate Development, Human Capital, Operations, and business leadership to align planning assumptions and financial outcomes.
- Advance FP&A systems, dashboards, data governance, automation, and reporting processes to improve timeliness, accuracy, and decision usefulness.
- Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain a high-performing FP&A team with strong analytical, business-partnering, and communication capabilities.

Role Expectations:

What You Will Do:

The Finance Director – Workday ERP Transformation will serve as the lead subject matter expert for the Workday Financial Management ERP tool in the Finance department. This highly visible role will drive the design and use of the Workday ERP tool within the organization, ensuring that business and control requirements translate into scalable Workday design decisions, and leverage the tool’s capabilities effectively.  This leader will guide the organization, and the finance department through the implementation, deployment, stabilization, and optimization of the Workday ERP tool and ensure alignment with associated business processes.

The Director will partner across Finance, Accounting, Technology, Data, Procurement, Human Capital, Operations, Internal Audit, and implementation teams to align Workday capabilities with enterprise processes and reporting needs. The successful candidate will bring deep Workday Financials expertise, including, ideally, knowledge of the PSA module.  Guidehouse is seeking a high-energy, hardworking leader who is deeply committed to and passionate about our mission, approaches colleagues and clients with humility and integrity, and thrives in a collaborative environment.

Key Responsibilities:

- Serve as the lead finance architect for the transition to Workday Financial Management, defining target-state, transition-state, and post-deployment architecture.
- Lead end-to-end solution design across the Workday Financials platform, including the Foundation Data Model, general ledger, accounting, revenue, customer accounts, supplier accounts, procurement, expenses, projects, assets, banking, settlements, budgeting, reporting, and analytics.
- Translate finance strategy, business requirements, accounting policies, internal controls, and reporting needs into scalable Workday configurations and architecture decisions.

- Own finance data conversion strategy, including data profiling, cleansing, mapping, transformation, reconciliation, historical data retention, cutover, and post-migration validation.
- Provide architectural oversight for integrations, banking, payroll, tax, procurement, expense, billing, planning, data warehouse, reporting, and other enterprise platforms.
- Establish finance design principles, documentation standards, governance forums, decision rights, and controls to maintain consistency across functional and technical workstreams.
- Lead design reviews and resolve complex ERP issues involving process standardization, localization, security, segregation of duties, data quality, performance, scalability, auditability, and regulatory compliance.
- Guide system integration testing, user acceptance testing, finance reconciliation, conversion validation, cutover planning, deployment readiness, hypercare, and stabilization.
- Partner with implementation vendors and internal teams to manage scope, dependencies, risks, issues, milestones, and architecture deliverables.
- Develop the post-implementation operating model, enhancement roadmap, release governance, support processes, and continuous improvement agenda for Workday Financials.

- Operate as a hands-on architect who can move effectively between enterprise strategy, detailed finance process design, system configuration, data, integrations, controls, testing, and issue resolution.
- Build trusted relationships with finance executives, accounting leaders, technology teams, business owners, and external implementation partners.
- Challenge unnecessary customization and promote standardized, sustainable processes while accounting for critical business and compliance requirements.
- Communicate complex architecture decisions, risks, trade-offs, and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Anticipate cross-functional ERP impacts and drive timely resolution of issues that could affect close, reporting, controls, business continuity, or implementation milestones.
- Maintain strong documentation, decision discipline, quality standards, and accountability throughout the transformation.
- Bring high energy and a strong work ethic to the transformation, demonstrating sustained commitment to and passion for Guidehouse’s mission while maintaining humility, integrity, and accountability.
- Foster a highly collaborative environment by actively listening, sharing credit, welcoming diverse perspectives, and partnering across functions to achieve collective outcomes.

What You Will Need:

- Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Information Systems, Business, or a related field.
- 12+ years of progressive finance, ERP, finance transformation, or enterprise systems experience, including leadership of complex implementations.
- Deep expertise in Workday architecture, configuration, business processes, security, reporting, integrations, and deployment methodology.
- Demonstrated experience serving as a Workday Financials architect or lead solution designer for a large-scale implementation or transformation.
- Required Workday ERP background with strong understanding of Workday finance processes, data structures, configuration, integrations, reporting, controls, and legacy-system dependencies.
- Workday Financial Management certifications or equivalent advanced implementation credentials.
- Proven experience transitioning from Peoplesoft or another complex legacy ERP to Workday, including architecture, data conversion, integration, testing, cutover, and stabilization activities.
- Broad understanding of ERP issues across accounting, financial reporting, planning, revenue, billing, procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, projects, expenses, assets, banking, tax, payroll, master data, security, and controls.
- Strong knowledge of finance operating models, U.S. GAAP, internal controls, segregation of duties, audit requirements, and data governance.

- Exceptional analytical, program leadership, stakeholder management, written communication, and presentation skills.

Our Financial Management Transformation professionals help our clients in Defense and National Security optimize all elements of their financial management structure by transforming business processes, enhancing operational efficiency, improving transparency and performance management, promoting change management, and complying with Federal laws and regulations.

The nature of our projects is extremely fluid and requires self-motivated individuals who are willing to develop solutions on their own or in a team of highly skilled professionals. - Creating performance metrics and interactive dashboards utilizing Microsoft Office Suite, Power Platform, SharePoint, Power BI, and more

- Collaborating with senior team members to embed financial management standards into the design and development of solutions, ensuring alignment with federal financial policies, audit readiness, and operational integrity

- Coordinating with other team members and/or building necessary skills to develop financial automation, data analytics, data visualization, and/or artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities for financial management use cases. This may include: building financial metrics and supporting dashboards utilizing data visualization software (i.e., Tableau, Power BI, etc.); building low-code applications and user interfaces (using PowerApps, Power Platforms, Appian, ServiceNow, etc.); building AI models to process and analyze high volumes of structured and unstructured financial data (using Databricks, Snowflake, Palantir, Python, R, SQL, etc.).

- Must be able to OBTAIN and MAINTAIN a Federal or DoD "PUBLIC TRUST"; candidates must obtain approved adjudication of their PUBLIC TRUST prior to onboarding with Guidehouse. Candidates with an ACTIVE PUBLIC TRUST or SUITABILITY are preferred.

- Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, accounting, information systems, engineering, business analytics, or a related field

- ONE (1) years of experience in business transformation, financial management, data analytics, audit or accounting.

- Experience with low-code and no-code technology platforms, including SharePoint, Power BI, Power Apps, Power Automate, and Tableau

- Ability to synthesize information quickly and learn new skills, view problems and apply a variety of solutions, and lead client-facing discussions and meetings

Experience with:
- Supporting client meetings and presenting recommendations to senior-level leadership

- Utilizing project management best practices

- Working in teams to produce high-impact work products

- Documenting and evaluating business processes and making recommendations for process improvements

- Conducting research to investigate client problems and working collaboratively with a team to formulate and recommend solutions

- Ability to develop insightful visualizations using Tableau, PowerBI or Qlik

We help our clients transform their business processes, improve efficiency of operations, evaluate and improve internal controls, strengthen policies and controls, increase transparency and performance management, and comply with Federal laws and regulations.

The nature of our projects can be fluid and requires self-motivated individuals that are willing to develop solutions on their own or in a team of highly skilled professionals. Project team members are provided the opportunity to interact with our clients’ senior management, as well as the opportunity to enhance their skills in the area of technical competency, business development, client service, leadership, project management, and people development.
This role will support a Government agency within the homeland security enterprise with opportunities to expand your support to other national security-related organizations. Specific initiatives and work products that this role supports include:

Responsibilities include:
- Transforming Financial Management (FM) processes with analytics & automation using emerging technologies: Design, build, and support data visualization (e.g., PowerBI/Tableau), low/no-code solutions (e.g., SharePoint/Power Platform), and/or AI/ML solutions (e.g., Databricks/Python) to modernize financial workflows and drive data-driven decisions for finance, accounting, budget, or risk management offices.

Is life sciences in your DNA?  Breakthroughs in pharma are helping people live healthier lives, while medical devices enable patients to proactively maintain health – this is undoubtedly a transformative time for health care companies. Guidehouse’s Life Sciences practice is an engine of innovation, helping pharmaceutical, biotech, medical device, and diagnostic companies develop custom solutions that tackle today’s challenges, while anticipating tomorrow’s. You will have an immediate impact by partnering with our clients, across all levels, to deliver product planning, pricing, reimbursement, product commercialization, and regulatory and compliance solutions.  Do you think you are up for the challenge?

We continuously strive to foster an inclusive and diverse work culture and thoughtfully develop our people through challenging work, valuable learning and educational programs. We cultivate a culture of mentorship and feedback for professional and personal growth. We help our clients take control of their future. This mission extends to our employee's careers, health and well-being and by the many ways we give back to our communities.

Associate Directors are responsible for managing projects from cultivation to completion.  In this role, you will lead the activities of the designated project team and support the day-to-day management of the client relationship. You will effectively develop and manage work plans, staffing, deadlines and budgets and manage multiple projects simultaneously. Your work products are high quality and client-ready.  In this visible role, you’ll lead team meetings and guide, manage, and coach staff consultants, providing constructive feedback on their project participation and overall career development. You will also collaborate with Directors and Managing Directors, keeping them abreast of project progress and important developments.  You will also take part in sales initiatives and practice development.  Travel is project dependent but averages 30 percent.

Guidehouse encourages career development and hiring for the long term.  Associate Directors follow a clearly defined career path.  As you hone your sales, project management skills, ability to manage multiple work streams, professional expertise, and meet client and business development goals, you will progress to the next level, Director.

- Strong understanding of the pharmaceutical industry, including drug development and launch.

- The ability to analyze complex information, identify key issues, and develop effective strategies.

- Experience in advising brand leaders, business unit leaders, and supporting insights & analytics leaders in pharma companies to support portfolio strategy, commercialization strategy and launch preparation efforts.

- Experience with doing projects around market sizing, HCP segmentation, patient journey, forecasting, brand strategy, commercial model design, sales force sizing, marketing mix and budget planning.

- Experience with key Pharma datasets – for example, CMS, EvaluatePharma, IQVIA/Symphony/Komodo claims, affiliations, Veeva activity data.

- Ability to work independently but with oversight from management. Experience in managing components of projects, ownership of workstreams and/or analytics and supervising, coaching or mentoring others in daily tasks is required.

- Excellent communication skills to convey strategic recommendations to various stakeholders, including senior management.

- Must possess strong analytical skills (Excel, Access, etc.) and leverage analytic techniques to use data to guide client and team decision-making.

- 5+ years of experience leading project engagements which includes planning, scoping, budget development, management and resource allocation, and managing multiple or more complex projects within scope, timeline and budget.

- 3+ years of formal management of team performance to achieve project goals and exceed client expectations.

- Must be willing and able to travel to client sites across the US, up to 30% of the time.

- Experience supporting affordable housing development, finance (ex. underwriting, lending, origination) or program implementation projects
